shouldFix.title: Frozen-review provenance is not bound to register round N
evidence: honestyRepairsKeyRule requires predecessorVerdictFindings[N] to be complete against the two frozen verdicts of round N, but provenanceCheck validates only the file chosen by the register entry: its path exists, its bytes match the entry's own sha256, and its verdict equals the entry's own verdict. No clause requires that chosen path be the canonical review for round N or that its digest equal the round/lane review pin in recordedInputs.

legacyVerdictOnlyReviews records round and reviewerLane alongside path and sha256, but terminalStatusCheck matches only path and sha256. The round and lane members are therefore not part of the eligibility predicate. pairCheck labels whatever files the register selected; it does not compare those selections to an external or canonical round map.

A concrete same-lane countermodel replaces predecessorVerdictFindings.v21.claude2 with the allowlisted v8 Claude path/hash/verdict and an empty findings array, and replaces the v21 Codex lane with the allowlisted v8 Codex path/hash/verdict and empty findings. Both exact hashes reproduce; both are statusless legacy-eligible; both verdicts are ACCEPT; Claude's combined findings=[] and Codex's empty severity arrays are recognized zero-finding schemas; ACCEPT iff 0/0 passes; lane identity remains Claude-to-Claude and Codex-to-Codex; the pair set and repaired-id set are both empty. Removing honestyRepairsFromV21 then satisfies every stated mechanical check while both actual frozen v21 REJECTs and their two SHOULD-FIX findings are ignored.

The subject's recordedInputs still contains the real v21 review paths and hashes, but neither provenanceCheck nor any other mechanical clause requires predecessorVerdictFindings.v21 to use those round-specific entries. Merely retaining unused correct pins does not defeat the substitution.

The live v22 data is clean: both registered v21 paths, hashes, COMPLETE statuses, REJECT verdicts, finding sets, dispositions, and repair prefixes reproduce exactly. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A successor can recycle earlier same-lane reviews—most sharply the recorded v8 dual ACCEPT pair—to fabricate a later round's dual ACCEPT and erase its actual blockers or SHOULD-FIX findings while every advertised provenance, terminal-status, verdict, extraction, pair, disposition, and repair-ledger check passes. This defeats the round-completeness guarantee that the register exists to provide.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Bind predecessorVerdictFindings[N][lane] to an explicit immutable round/lane review identity before extraction. At minimum require its path to equal the canonical host-effect-authorization.vN.review-independent.<lane>.json path and its sha256 to equal the corresponding recordedInputs pin; where review schema exposes subject/reviewOf and reviewer identity, require those to match N and lane as well. For legacy eligibility, match the full (round, reviewerLane, path, sha256) tuple in legacyVerdictOnlyReviews, not path+sha256 alone. Any cross-round or cross-lane substitution MUST refuse.
